rv.q: Laiona Michelle's tribute to Nina Simone, 'Little Girl Blue,' which recently opened at New World Stages, fits the general format, with some interesting, if not always successfully implemented, idiosyncratic touches.
Little Girl Blue is a grand showcase for Laiona Michelle and a powerful affirmation of Nina Simone.
Though Little Girl Blue (also the title of Simone's first album) feels crammed with more biography than it can comfortably contain, Michelle's performance holds us.

What Little Girl Blue, named after Simone's debut album, fails to do is celebrate a complex personality, a nuanced human being, and a proud Black woman who could not — and never wanted to — be put in a box.
"Michelle largely captures the essence of an exceedingly complex woman, avoiding outright copy-catting in this dazzling stage performance.

cn.t: Laiona Michelle's biographical musical earns praise for her powerhouse performance channeling Nina Simone, though critics split on whether the show adequately captures the icon's complexity beyond a well-executed concert tribute.
